conforming-control.json.reason: a body fully covered by the declared schema is accepted at the producer (tiers 1-4 all pass) and interpretable by the reader

undeclared-field.json.reason: rule 3: a field the schema declares no rule for is a producer rejection; a reader tolerates it, folding the op and ignoring the unrecognized field

value-type-mismatch.json.reason: rule 3: a value failing its declared value_type is a producer rejection; the read path does no value typing (spec/value-types.md), so the reader folds the op with the value intact

undeclared-op-type.json.reason: rule 4: an op_type the schema does not declare for this object_type is a producer rejection; a reader has no matching rule and reports UnknownOp

undeclared-op-version.json.reason: rule 4: an op_version the schema does not declare for this op_type is a producer rejection; a reader has no matching rule and reports UnknownOp

undeclared-object-type.json.reason: tier 4: an object_type no schema in the log declares is refused at the producer; a reader falls through the absent-schema path to UnknownOp (FC-1, spec/schema-ops.md 7.1)

contested-object-type.json.reason: tier 3 (the ruling's carve-out): two schema objects binding the same bare object_type install no rules (spec/schema-ops.md 6), so the write is permitted unvalidated while the reader still reports UnknownOp -- the write/read asymmetry is the point

declared-type-with-no-fields.json.reason: tier 2 is decided from the declared-type set, not from a non-empty rules slice: a type declared by define-op alone (no define-field) accepts an op of its declared op type with an empty body; with no field rules installed at all, a reader has nothing to fold and reports UnknownOp

deprecated-field-still-writable.json.reason: deprecated is metadata discouraging new writes, never a filter (spec/schema-ops.md 5, 8): the field rule stays installed and active for both the producer and the fold

keyed-lww-key-column.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214): a keyed-lww field's key column is declared by being a member of key on the field's own rule, not by a separate field rule of its own, so a body carrying both the field and its key column is accepted at the producer and interpretable by the reader

keyed-lww-key-column-not-a-string.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214): a keyed-lww key column's value MUST be a JSON string regardless of its key_types entry, because fold treats a non-string key component as uninterpretable (spec/fold.md §5 keyed-lww); this is the lockstep pin -- a producer refusal matched by a reader quarantine, not the interpretable-but-wrong tolerance an ordinary value_type mismatch gets

keyed-lww-key-column-null.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 2): JSON null is not a JSON string, so a keyed-lww key column carrying null is rejected the same as any other non-string key column value -- unlike an ordinary declared field, where null is tolerated as a legitimate 'no write', a key column addresses a register rather than carrying a value of its own and fold's keyed-lww strategy does not tolerate null there either

keyed-lww-key-column-enum.json.reason: rule 3 (WRIT-214 round 2): an enum-typed key column is held to the JSON-string requirement and nothing more, because key_types (a column -> catalogue type name map) has no slot for the member list an enum field's own enum attribute would supply -- accepting a value outside any particular field's declared enum members is correct here, not a hole, since key_types carries no member list to check membership against in the first place
